intro: A link sends three data bits and one extra bit. Choose the extra bit so the receiver counts an even or odd total number of ones.

questions.title: Build an even word
questions.prompt: The transmitter sends 101 in even mode. Which parity bit completes the word?
questions.feedback: 101 contains two ones. Appending 0 gives 1010, which still contains two ones.

questions.title: Change the mode
questions.prompt: Keep the data at 101 and select odd mode. What happens to the parity bit?
questions.feedback: Only odd_mode changed. XOR with 1 flips the output, giving 1011 with three ones.

questions.title: Read the board
questions.prompt: SW2…SW0 read 111 and SW3 is up (odd mode). What should LD0 show?
questions.feedback: 111 already has three ones. A parity bit of 0 preserves odd parity, so LD0 is off.
